steps.tx: Pathological enlargement, downward displacement, and vascular engorgement of normal anal cushions produce **haemorrhoids**. These vascular cushions reside within the submucosa of the anal canal at the classic three, seven, and eleven o'clock positions in the lithotomy view. Straining, chronic constipation, and elevated intra-abdominal pressure disrupt the supporting Treitz muscle and elastic framework, leading to painless bright red rectal bleeding coating the stool surface.
steps.say: Haemorrhoids represent displaced, engorged anal cushions located at three, seven, and eleven o'clock that bleed painlessly with defecation.

vis.alt: Cross-sectional anatomical diagram illustrating Goligher internal haemorrhoid grading from grades one through four.
vis.caption: Haemorrhoid classification: anatomical grading of internal haemorrhoid prolapse relative to the anal sphincter. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Internal haemorrhoids situated above the dentate line are classified into four distinct severity levels by **Goligher internal haemorrhoid grading**. Grade one haemorrhoids bleed but never prolapse outside the anal canal. Grade two prolapse through the anal verge during defecation but reduce spontaneously. Grade three require manual reduction back into the canal, whereas grade four are permanently prolapsed, non-reducible, and prone to thrombosis and strangulation.
steps.say: Goligher staging classifies internal haemorrhoids from grade one bleeding without prolapse to grade four irreducible prolapse.

steps.tx: The most widely performed outpatient procedural intervention for symptomatic grade two and selected grade three haemorrhoids is **rubber band ligation**. An elastic ligature is deployed around the apex of the redundant vascular cushion at least one centimetre above the dentate line. The band arrests arterial inflow, provoking ischemic necrosis and sloughing within five to seven days while producing scarring that anchors the cushion to the underlying muscularis.
steps.say: Rubber band ligation arrests mucosal blood supply above the dentate line, causing ischemic sloughing and scar fixation.

nodes.label: Grasping Mucosa 1 to 2 cm Above Dentate Line
Firing Elastic Ligature around Mucosal Pedicle

steps.tx: A non-excisional surgical technique designed to correct mucosal prolapse without creating external perianal wounds is **stapled haemorrhoidopexy**. Known as the Longo procedure, a circular endo-anal stapler excises a circumferential ring of redundant rectal mucosa and submucosa four centimetres above the dentate line. This simultaneously interrupts the superior rectal vascular pedicles and hitches the prolapsed cushions back into their anatomical position with significantly reduced postoperative pain.
steps.say: Stapled haemorrhoidopexy excises a mucosal ring above the dentate line, repositioning cushions and reducing postoperative pain.

left.title: Stapled Haemorrhoidopexy (Longo)
points: Circumferential mucosal excision above dentate line
No sensitive perianal skin wounds created

right.title: Open Excisional Haemorrhoidectomy
points: Direct surgical excision of all three vascular cushions
Open perineal wounds left to granulate
Lowest lifetime risk of haemorrhoid recurrence

steps.tx: The definitive surgical gold standard procedure for severe grade four, strangulated, or mixed internal-external haemorrhoids is **open haemorrhoidectomy**. Under the Milligan-Morgan technique, each of the three primary vascular cushions is dissected off the internal anal sphincter up to its vascular pedicle and securely ligated. Crucially, intervening bridges of healthy anoderm and mucous membrane are preserved to prevent postoperative anal stenosis.
steps.say: Milligan-Morgan open haemorrhoidectomy excises vascular cushions while preserving mucocutaneous skin bridges to avoid anal canal stenosis.

vis.alt: Surgical operative view of Milligan-Morgan open excisional haemorrhoidectomy showing triangular skin bridges left between excised cushions.
vis.caption: Open haemorrhoidectomy: Milligan-Morgan technique leaving open mucocutaneous bridges between excision sites. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: A longitudinal tear or painful linear ulcer in the squamoepithelial lining of the lower anal canal distal to the dentate line is an **anal fissure**. Over ninety percent of fissures occur in the posterior midline, where the elliptical arrangement of external sphincter fibers leaves the anal wall poorly supported. Passage of hard, bulky scybalous stool tears the fragile anoderm, provoking intense knife-like pain during and after defecation.
steps.say: An anal fissure is a tear in the posterior midline anoderm causing intense burning pain during and following defecation.

nodes.label: Passage of Hard Stool or Explosive Diarrhea
Mechanical Tear in Posterior Midline Anoderm
Severe Reflex Spasm of Internal Anal Sphincter

steps.tx: The self-perpetuating cycle that converts an acute mucosal tear into a non-healing chronic fissure is **internal anal sphincter spasm**. Pain triggers reflex hypertonicity of the involuntary internal sphincter, elevating resting anal canal pressure well above eighty millimeters of mercury. This muscular spasm compresses the entering posterior microvessels, creating severe relative ischemia at the posterior commissure that arrests epithelial regeneration.
steps.say: Internal anal sphincter spasm produces severe local microvascular ischemia, preventing spontaneous healing of the posterior fissure.

left.title: Acute Anal Fissure
points: Duration under six weeks from onset
Superficial mucosal tear with fresh red edges
High rate of healing with conservative measures

right.title: Chronic Anal Fissure
points: Persisting beyond six to eight weeks
Indurated margins with visible white sphincter fibers
Features sentinel skin tag and hypertrophied papilla

steps.tx: The definitive surgical procedure of choice for chronic anal fissure refractory to pharmacological therapy is **lateral internal sphincterotomy**. Performed either open or closed, the surgeon carefully divides the distal one-third of the hypertonic internal anal sphincter muscle in the lateral quadrant away from the fissure. This permanently relieves internal sphincter spasm, restores posterior mucosal perfusion, and promotes rapid fissure healing in over ninety-five percent of cases.
steps.say: Lateral internal sphincterotomy divides the distal internal sphincter, permanently abolishing spasm and enabling fissure healing.

rows: Surgical division of lower internal sphincter

steps.tx: The preferred initial conservative medical approach for both acute and chronic fissures is pharmacological **chemical sphincterotomy**. Topical application of two percent diltiazem ointment or 0.2 percent glyceryl trinitrate to the anal margin achieves reversible smooth muscle relaxation of the internal sphincter. This reduces resting anal pressure and enhances posterior blood flow without inducing the permanent sphincter damage associated with surgical cut.
steps.say: Chemical sphincterotomy with topical calcium channel blockers relaxes the internal sphincter, achieving high healing rates without permanent incontinence.

nodes.label: Twice Daily Topical 2% Diltiazem or GTN Ointment
